O.outcome_detail: Pre-course, in-class, and post-course preventive medicine test scores

cells.quote: Statistical analysis revealed that the intervention group consistently outperformed the control group on the pre-course, in-class, and post-course tests (p < 0.01). The differences in the test scores between the intervention and control groups gradually increased when moving from the pre-intervention to mid-intervention to post-intervention tests (F = 23.615, p = 0.001) (Mauchly’s test confirmed that the assumption of sphericity was met; therefore, unadjusted F values were reported), as shown in Tables 2, 3.
cells.note: The two intact classes were selected nonrandomly; the post-course test was administered 1 week after the course ended, but timing across the three tests was not uniform.

O.outcome_detail: Student Engagement Scale total learning score and dimensions

cells.quote: The analysis of the questionnaire data revealed significant differences between the two groups. Specifically, the total learning scores of the students in the intervention group was higher (58.69 ± 11.34) than that in the control group (50.96 ± 10.09) (t = 3.997, p = 0.003). The students in the intervention group presented high-performance scores in the three dimensions of learning emotions, learning engagement, and learning performance (p < 0.0083), as shown in Table 4 and Supplementary Table S1.
cells.note: The SES measured learning methods, emotions, engagement, and performance; questionnaire administration timing relative to the intervention was not stated.
